# Chronicle of the fictional northern districts

Source: Elian Voss, compiled chronicle, 1908 fictional edition.
Source stance: the compiler favours the estate officers and sometimes quotes
the earlier traveller Mara Quill.

In 1712 three independent Northwatch companies were raised at Dunbrae to guard
the hill roads. Two more companies joined them in 1718. In 1720 the five
companies were mustered as the Northwatch Regiment. Their dark blue coats led
local speakers to call them "An Freiceadan Gorm", meaning the Blue Watch.

The House of Rannoch held farms in Glen Mora. The district of Rannoch and the
title Earl of Rannoch are distinct from the House of Rannoch, although the
chronicle often shortens all three to "Rannoch".

Voss states that Factor Iven warned the Glen Mora tenants before the 1841
removals and argues that the estate acted lawfully. Mara Quill's quoted diary
instead describes families reaching the coast without shelter. These are
opposed source stances about the same removals, not a resolved fact about blame.

The phrase "Children of the Rain" does not occur in this chronicle. A later
summary calls the displaced House of Brannoch landless hill fugitives, which may
suggest why a nickname arose but does not directly evidence that exact phrase.
